question.text: Whole life insurance policies were originally popular in India primarily for which of the following reasons?

answer.text: They were designed to pass wealth to the next generation without payment of estate duty, because life insurance death payments were normally exempt from estate duty; with estate duty abolished, they should be evaluated like other investment-cum-insurance policies
They offered the highest investment returns among all life insurance products due to lifelong compounding
They were the only type of policy that offered tax benefits under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act
They were mandatory for all government employees as part of their employment benefits package

explanation.text: The Logic: Whole life policies were originally designed primarily to pass wealth to the next generation without payment of estate duty, since life insurance death payments were normally exempt from estate duty. With estate duty since abolished in India, whole life policies should now be evaluated on the same footing as other investment-cum-insurance policies. The Trap: "Highest investment returns" is incorrect — whole life policies typically have lower returns than endowment plans of equivalent premium due to longer coverage periods and higher cumulative mortality charges. They were never mandatory for government employees, and Section 80C benefits are not unique to whole life. Note: Even after estate duty was abolished, whole life policies can still play a role in legacy planning and providing for dependents with lifelong needs — but they should be compared on cost and return basis against other investment-cum-insurance products.
